areas.title: Perovskite Solar Cells
description: Research on perovskite solar cells examines film formation, charge transport, and interfacial recombination in relation to device efficiency and stability. Crystallization studies include delayed thermal annealing with halide additives, cesium-assisted two-step deposition, and preheating followed by moderate-temperature liquid-medium annealing. Device studies cover chemically deposited SnO₂ on mesoporous TiO₂ electrodes, dopant-free and fluorinated hole-transport materials, energy-level alignment, carrier extraction, and scalable coating methods such as blade and bar coating.

Reliability studies evaluate perovskite devices under combined illumination, heat, vacuum, and radiation. PVDF-HFP modification is used to study film and interface stability, while proton-irradiation and two-terminal tandem-cell studies examine degradation under space-relevant conditions. These studies connect device performance with scalable processing and reliability testing under terrestrial and space-relevant environments.

areas.title: Redox Flow Batteries
description: Research on vanadium redox flow batteries examines electrode reaction kinetics, electrolyte transport, and cycling efficiency. Graphite-felt electrodes are modified with nanostructured graphitic carbon nitride to introduce nitrogen-rich active sites and improve electrolyte contact. Electrochemical measurements are used to evaluate the VO²⁺/VO₂⁺ and V²⁺/V³⁺ reactions, polarization, charge transfer, and the permeability required for electrolyte circulation.

Separator studies focus on proton or ion transport, vanadium crossover, and stability in acidic electrolytes. Metal–organic frameworks and covalent organic frameworks are evaluated as porous components in composite membranes, where pore structure and surface chemistry affect selectivity and transport resistance. Current work combines graphite-felt surface modification and membrane design with electrochemical testing of reaction kinetics, crossover, and cycling stability.

areas.title: Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells
description: Research on dye-sensitized solar cells examines how photoanode structure, interfaces, electrolyte transport, and fabrication conditions affect charge generation and collection. Studies include branched and tetrapod-like ZnO nanostructures, microporous TiO₂ electrodes, ionic-liquid diffusion, gel-polymer electrolytes, and mesoscopic conducting-polymer counter electrodes. These experiments relate electrode morphology and pore structure to dye adsorption, electron transport, charge-transfer resistance, and device stability.

Flexible and large-area devices were studied through titanium-substrate interfacial layers, repeated electrophoretic deposition, low-temperature processing, sealing, and electrolyte-retention control. Mesoporous SiO₂ decoration was also evaluated in bifacial and back-illuminated cells. These studies clarified how electrode structure, deposition conditions, and electrolyte transport affect flexible cells and large-area DSSC modules.
